$comment: Rule catalog — concurrency. Standard 52. One rule, deliberately: races, assumed atomicity, and unsynchronized shared state are one failure family with one remedy. Duplicate-on-retry routes to Standard 13.

rules.title: Shared mutable state has defined synchronization behaviour
rules.description: No state reachable from more than one execution context is left without a stated rule about how those contexts interleave, no operation is assumed atomic that is not, and no known race is left unrecorded.
rules.rationale: One rule for three prohibitions because they are one failure: code assuming an interleaving the runtime never promised. Splitting them would produce three findings for one defect and three not-evaluated entries for a project with no concurrency at all.
rules.remediation: State the synchronization rule — a lock, a queue, a transaction isolation level, immutability, single ownership, or a compare-and-swap. Defined as unnecessary, because the value is immutable, is a valid definition; undefined is the violation.
rules.$assuranceNote: Whether state is shared depends on how the code is invoked, which is not visible where it is defined; whether synchronization is adequate depends on the invariant being protected, which is not in the code at all.
